title: 16 December Instrument of Surrender
subtitle: 16 December 1971, Dhaka
summary: On 16 December 1971, Lieutenant General A. A. K. Niazi signed the Instrument of Surrender at Dhaka’s Ramna Racecourse, accepted by Lieutenant General Jagjit Singh Aurora, the General Officer Commanding-in-Chief of the Indian and Bangladesh forces in the eastern theatre. Banglapedia gives the signing time as 5:01 p.m. without specifying a time zone; a contemporaneous Indian parliamentary announcement gives 16:31 Indian Standard Time, and Keesing’s 1972 account gives 4:31 p.m. without specifying a time zone. Accounts therefore differ. Banglapedia states that Group Captain A. K. Khandaker, deputy chief of staff of the Bangladesh forces, represented the Mukti Bahini.
heroTagline: The surrender ceremony at Ramna Racecourse
whyItMatters: The instrument fixed the military outcome of the war and ended Pakistani command in the east. The date is commemorated as Victory Day, while reconstruction and the consequences of wartime violence continued.

claimCitations.claim: On 16 December 1971, Lieutenant General A. A. K. Niazi signed the Instrument of Surrender at Dhaka’s Ramna Racecourse, accepted by Lieutenant General Jagjit Singh Aurora, the General Officer Commanding-in-Chief of the Indian and Bangladesh forces in the eastern theatre. Banglapedia gives 5:01 p.m. without a time zone; a contemporaneous Indian parliamentary announcement gives 16:31 IST; Keesing’s 1972 account gives 4:31 p.m. without a time zone. Accounts differ. Banglapedia states that Group Captain A. K. Khandaker, deputy chief of staff of the Bangladesh forces, represented the Mukti Bahini.

The instrument fixed the military outcome of the war and ended Pakistani command in the east. The date is commemorated as Victory Day, while reconstruction and the consequences of wartime violence continued.
The surrender remains a primary documentary marker of Bangladesh’s victory and is commemorated annually on 16 December.
